bank.title: RCET 3373 Advanced Computer Architecture and Embedded Systems Theory
bank.description: Fall 2026 working theory question pool for the first three weeks. Starter items require instructor review before graded use.

questions.stem: What unsigned decimal value is represented by `0xAD`?
Interpret `11111011` as an 8-bit two's-complement integer.
questions.solution: The pattern is the 8-bit two's-complement representation of -5.

questions.stem: A driver guarantees `VOH >= 4.2 V` and a receiver requires `VIH >= 3.5 V`. What is the HIGH-state noise margin?
questions.solution: NMH = VOH(min) - VIH(min) = 4.2 - 3.5 = 0.7 V.

questions.stem: Which statement is most accurate about a measured digital HIGH?

choices.text: It must equal the supply voltage exactly
It is an analog voltage that is interpreted as HIGH when it satisfies the receiver's guaranteed input requirement
It has no relationship to voltage
It is valid whenever it is above half the supply voltage

questions.solution: Digital interpretation is based on specified voltage regions and conditions, not an exact ideal voltage or a universal half-supply rule.

questions.stem: What is the period of a 10 kHz waveform in microseconds?
A device requires 20 ns setup and 10 ns hold. Data is stable 35 ns before the clock edge but changes 8 ns after it. Which statement is correct?
questions.solution: 35 ns exceeds the 20 ns setup requirement, but 8 ns does not meet the 10 ns hold requirement.

questions.stem: Match the information type with its role in a digital transaction.
Match each general memory category with a typical role.

pairs.target: Occasionally changed data that should survive power loss

questions.stem: Using `ideal step = range / 2^N`, what is the ideal step size in millivolts for an 8-bit converter covering 0 to 5 V?

source.document: AN693 Understanding A/D Converter Performance Specifications

questions.stem: A converter with more bits is automatically more accurate in every practical measurement system.
questions.solution: More bits improve ideal resolution, but total accuracy also depends on reference error, offset/gain/nonlinearity, noise, acquisition/source behavior, and other system effects.

source.document: AN693 Understanding A/D Converter Performance Specifications

questions.stem: Which source should be treated as the primary authority for the PIC16F883-specific reset value and bit definition of an SFR?

choices.text: The current PIC16F883 family device datasheet

questions.solution: Device-specific register definitions should be checked against the current device datasheet.

questions.stem: What hexadecimal program-memory address is the PIC16F883 reset vector? Enter the numeric value.
questions.solution: The reset vector is at program-memory address 0x0000.

questions.stem: What hexadecimal program-memory address is the PIC16F883 interrupt vector? Enter the numeric value.
questions.solution: The interrupt vector is at program-memory address 0x0004.

questions.stem: Match each source element with its role.

pairs.target: CPU instruction that changes program flow
Assembler/linker directive describing a code section

source.document: MPLAB XC8 PIC Assembler User's Guide

questions.stem: Match the register category with its typical role.
What is the main purpose of `BANKSEL TRISB` in readable PIC-AS source?

choices.text: It sets every TRISB bit to input
It emits the bank-selection operations needed so a following file-register access refers to TRISB

questions.solution: BANKSEL is assembler support for selecting the bank containing the named register; the following instruction still performs the register read/write.

source.document: MPLAB XC8 PIC Assembler User's Guide

questions.stem: For the PIC16F883 TRIS direction registers, a bit value of 1 configures the corresponding port pin as an input and 0 as an output.
questions.solution: The PIC16F883 I/O documentation uses 1=input and 0=output for TRIS bits.

questions.stem: A PIC pin intended for digital I/O is still configured for an analog function. Which is the best first response?

choices.text: Use the datasheet to identify and configure the analog-selection controls for that pin

questions.solution: Multifunction pins must be configured for the intended function. The datasheet's I/O/analog-selection documentation is the authority.

questions.stem: Place these checks in a reasonable early troubleshooting order when the device programs successfully but a digital output does not behave as expected.
items: Confirm the programmed build/source is the intended one
Confirm power reset and clock assumptions
Check TRIS direction and target register/bank
Confirm the physical pin and measurement connection
questions.solution: The course emphasizes evidence-first diagnosis before random source edits or rewiring.

questions.stem: For the course's classic mid-range PIC timing model, `FOSC = 8 MHz`. What is `TCY` in microseconds?
questions.solution: TOSC = 1/8 MHz = 0.125 us. TCY = 4*TOSC = 0.5 us.

source.document: PICmicro Mid-Range MCU Family Reference Manual

questions.stem: At `FOSC = 4 MHz`, a symmetric loop changes RB0 once every 4 instruction cycles. What is the full waveform period in microseconds?
questions.solution: At 4 MHz, TCY=1 us. One transition interval is 4 us; a complete HIGH+LOW period is 8 us.

questions.stem: A loop is `DECFSZ count,1` followed by `GOTO Loop`, with count initially N. Using 1 cycle for a normal DECFSZ, 2 cycles when it skips, and 2 cycles for GOTO, how many loop-body cycles occur for N=4? Do not include setup instructions.
questions.solution: Three normal iterations cost 3 cycles each, and the final skip iteration costs 2: 3*3+2=11 cycles, equivalent to 3N-1.

questions.stem: A student calculates a DECFSZ/GOTO loop by multiplying every iteration by 3 cycles, including the final one.
prompts: Explain why the final iteration is different.
State the loop-body formula for N iterations using the documented cycle counts.
answers: When DECFSZ reaches zero it takes the skip path and the GOTO does not execute.

questions.stem: Order the conceptual actions of a normal subroutine call and return.
items: CALL preserves the return address on the hardware return stack
Program Counter changes to the subroutine destination
RETURN retrieves the most recent saved return address
Program Counter resumes at the caller

source.document: PICmicro Mid-Range MCU Family Reference Manual

questions.stem: Which instruction returns from a subroutine and also loads W with a literal value?
questions.solution: RETLW returns and loads W with the literal encoded in the instruction.

questions.stem: A student records a symmetric waveform with 50 us HIGH, 50 us LOW, a 100 us period, and a displayed frequency of 20 kHz. Which value is inconsistent with the others?
questions.solution: A 100 us period corresponds to 10 kHz, so the 20 kHz frequency is inconsistent.

questions.stem: Why can the exact instruction-cycle timing of an embedded C loop usually not be determined from the C source alone?

choices.text: The compiler, optimization settings, target, and generated machine instructions determine the executed path
C always executes one instruction per source line
Only an oscilloscope can determine any timing

questions.solution: Cycle-accurate timing belongs to the machine instructions that actually execute; compiler output and optimization can change that implementation.
